- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and prices are rising, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 2-period moving average.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.1–0.3) and history shows mean reversion, model often fails to revert; apply 1–2% downward correction toward prior 5-day average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth with 3-period moving average or use sentiment-weighted average (higher weight for recent sentiment).  
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.0–0.1) and prices are rising, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to capture “quiet bullish” bias.
